paradigm.title: 1. Why get an AI search audit now? (A paradigm shift)
paradigm.lead: Search results are no longer ten blue links.
paradigm.body: ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews summarize the question and answer it immediately. Users finish buying, inquiring, or booking without visiting a site. The real question is no longer “Are we found?” but “Does AI understand, trust, and cite our brand?” Without a diagnosis now, you keep buying ads while missing the traffic path that already changed.

points.0: Generative search completes the answer before the click. If you are not in the citation list, the demand itself disappears.
points.1: Classic SEO (keywords and backlinks) still matters, but without machine-readable signals you can rank and still never be recommended.
points.2: First-mover effects compound. Brands indexed as citation sources are more likely to reappear in later answers.

schema.title: 2. Why SEO & GEO Schema.org patches matter — and what changes after
schema.lead: Schema.org JSON-LD is the standard language that lets search engines and AI identify your company instead of guessing.
schema.body: Human-readable copy alone rarely gives AI enough confidence about your organization, services, location, FAQs, or author credibility. If types such as Organization, WebSite, Article, FAQ, Product, and LocalBusiness — and their required fields — are missing, AI prefers a competitor page or Wikipedia as the safer source. A schema patch turns visibility from a hope into a machine-verifiable fact.

before.0: HTML exists, but the entity (who / what) stays ambiguous.
before.1: You fall short of rich-result and knowledge-panel eligibility.
before.2: AI assigns low source confidence when deciding whether to cite you.

after.0: Brand, services, and location lock in as machine-readable identifiers.
after.1: Answer-shaped content such as FAQ/HowTo becomes easier to extract and cite.
after.2: Technical SEO scores and GEO citation likelihood rise together.

geo.title: 3. Why you need GEO (AI search visibility) optimization
geo.lead: GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) aims to keep your site as a cited source inside AI answers.
geo.body: The core signals are AI-crawler access, E-E-A-T (experience, expertise, authoritativeness, trust), author/publisher profiles, and content where claims map to evidence. Ranking on page one still fails if you never appear in the AI answer — at the moment of decision, you do not exist. GEO is not buying more ads. It is the technical investment that puts you in the answer set AI chooses.

points.0: Crawlers such as GPTBot and PerplexityBot must be able to collect your content before you can be a training or citation candidate.
points.1: Clear authors, publishing organization, contact details, and source evidence make you a safer citation against hallucination.
points.2: To be recommended on category + location + problem queries without your brand name, schema and content signals have to reinforce each other.

If the score is low, you are already losing the 90% of new conversational explorers who do not know your name — all of them go to competitors.

risks.title: 5. 🚨 Three risks of skipping GEO optimization
risks.lead: Delaying GEO is not a marketing task you can “do later.” AI search share accumulates, and empty slots are filled by competitors.

0.title: Invisibility in AI search
0.body: Users finish buying, inquiring, or booking from the AI answer alone. If you are not cited, organic traffic structurally declines and the site becomes a ghost brand behind the results.

1.title: Category brand substitution
1.body: When the same question repeats, AI reinforces the competitor it already cited as the category answer. Once their name is locked into the reply, ads rarely reverse that perception.

2.title: Recovery cost that compounds
2.body: Even if you later add schema and E-E-A-T, reversing learned preference takes more content and authority signals. Filling that gap with ads usually costs more than the technical patch would have.

rag.chunkIntro: One chunk = one question. Write [Question ➔ Direct answer ➔ 3 proofs] so AI can copy the first line.

rules.1: Keep each chunk at 500–800 characters including spaces. Do not mix questions in one chunk.
rules.2: [Question] should be the long-tail location + service prompt a consumer would ask AI.
rules.3: [Direct answer] put the brand and conclusion in sentence one; facts before adjectives.
rules.4: [Proofs 1–3] use only verifiable facts: location, credentials, and published results.

chunk.a: [Direct answer] Example: '''{Brand} is located in {location} and officially provides {service}.'''
chunk.p1: [Proof 1] Present verifiable figures such as certifications, genuine equipment, and principal licenses
chunk.p2: [Proof 2] State the official road-name address, hours, parking, and reservation system
chunk.p3: [Proof 3] Combine FAQPage schema with an official website URL source link
